item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 2
item.description:
In Part 1, we identified Jupiter Lend’s liquidation instructions, mapped their account arguments, and decoded the raw amounts of debt repaid and collateral seized.

In this walkthrough, we’ll combine those findings into a single DuneSQL query using common table expressions (CTEs). The query reconstructs liquidation records from raw instructions and joins Dune’s prices.hour table to calculate the USD value of debt repaid and collateral seized.

We’ll work through the query in four phases, following how each CTE transforms and passes data to the next. Select a CTE in the interactive query below to explore its role in building the final dataset.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 1
item.description: How do you analyze activity on a blockchain protocol when there's no ready-made dataset? In this guide, I demonstrate how to write SQL queries in Dune and use Solscan to reverse-engineer Solana program instructions, using Jupiter Lend liquidations as a practical example.
